subject: general
question: What is the process of transport of soluble products of photosynthesis and other materials from the leaves to other tissues of the plant called?
solution:
The correct answer is "__**Translocation**__".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Translocation** is the transport of substances within the plant from leaves to other tissues.
 
• While photosynthesis allows plants to manufacture **carbohydrates** (sugars) in their leaves, other organic and inorganic substances are also needed by nonphotosynthetic plant components.
 
• Because of this, **nutrients** are moved from sources (areas with a surplus of carbohydrates, typically mature leaves) to sinks (regions where the carbohydrate is needed).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Roots, flowers, fruits, stems**, and emerging leaves are a few significant sinks.
 
• As sources later, when they are roughly halfway developed, **leaves** are particularly fascinating because they are sinks while they are young.
